summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable (simulation_allowed=false, comparison_valid=false). Studio did not run; the simulation status is skipped because the custom experiment has no blocks and no power_w object. The scenario is a 4-layer TSV-based 3D stack (GSRC n100, FP1/FP2, Figure 9 with Figure 6 correlation context), evaluated with HotSpot steady-state peak temperature against a power-based thermal goodness value (TGV). The proposed experiment kind was custom_2d_steady, which has no transient trace and would not represent vertical inter-layer coupling or TSV islands. Block geometry, per-block powers, and HotSpot configuration are unpublished. No Studio output exists, so no numerical comparison with the paper is possible or valid. The only paper temperatures are 564 K and 567 K from Figure 10. They are whole-stack HotSpot peaks, and their identity with the Figure 9 FP1/FP2 is unconfirmed. Qualitatively, the paper reports layer 0, farthest from the top heat sink, as the hottest layer. It also reports that TGV correlates with HotSpot peak temperature (r=0.89 for n100, 0.96 across all GSRC benchmarks). These are paper-reported findings, not results reproduced here. The gate also records unresolved adversarial and independent-review checks and evidence entries lacking valid page or asset locators. No claim of replication or agreement can be made.
